notes: Status is recomputed by scripts/check_release_readiness.py. Automated gates are re-derived from the repository and are never read from this file.
Evidence expires when a file it declares under 'covers' changes between its recorded commit and HEAD. Evidence with no 'covers' expires on any commit change.

0.1.0a3 was published on 2026-09-06 and verified on PyPI. Its gate evidence is preserved in docs/releases/history/0.1.0a3.md and is deliberately not carried here as satisfied: 0.1.0a4 must re-establish it against its own candidate commit.

RELEASE_PLAN.md states the first 0.1.0a4 gate as one automated gate, "Every 0.1.0a3 gate still satisfied". It is decomposed here into the individual 0.1.0a3 gates, because the checker requires every automated gate to have a real implementation and an aggregate over sibling gates would be circular.
0.1.0a4 is not ready and no gate specific to it is satisfied. Its evidence depends on reference applications built outside this repository, which will be audited separately.

ADR 0068 inserts 0.1.0a5 between 0.1.0a4 and 0.1.0b1 and fixes what each release owns. Only the current target carries gates in this file; the 0.1.0a5 and 0.1.0b1 gates live in RELEASE_PLAN.md until their target becomes current.

ADR 0071 gives agnara-http a public composition API, removing the second repository blocker docs/releases/STATUS.md recorded. The two HTTP gates stay unsatisfied: they are evidence about external applications, which still need building, and adapter distributions are still unpublished (Issue #291).

gates.title: Reference applications exist and install Agnara as an ordinary dependency
gates.detail: Applications are being built externally in agnara-project. Note that only agnara is published to PyPI: an application needing HTTP or MCP cannot install an adapter as an ordinary dependency today.

gates.title: No reference application imports Agnara internals
gates.detail: agnara-http declares a public composition API (ADR 0071) and every shipped distribution's public surface is now classified in docs/public-api.json (ADR 0076), so this gate is decidable rather than a matter of review: scripts/check_public_imports.py audits any tree, inside or outside this workspace, and reports every import that names an unclassified module or pulls an unclassified name out of a classified one. It runs green today on examples/, README.md, the guides under docs/ and the CLI's generated projects. The gate stays unsatisfied because it is evidence about applications built outside this workspace, and those do not exist yet.

gates.title: No reference application requires a monkey patch
gates.detail: No evidence can exist until the reference applications being built in agnara-project are complete and audited.

gates.title: Public APIs are sufficient to build the reference applications
gates.detail: A maintainer decides this after the applications are audited. The manifest now classifies 280 exports across 47 public modules in all seven distributions, and the release gate rejects any newly unclassified package or leaf module in any of them (ADR 0074, ADR 0076). agnara-cli dropped 13 undocumented implementation helpers from its public surface in the same change. HTTP JSON bodies materialize standard-library dataclasses at the transport boundary before strict core validation (ADR 0075). Sufficiency itself remains unproven: no application has been built against this surface.

gates.title: HTTP exposure works from an application
gates.detail: The supported path exists: RFC 0006 is answered by ADR 0070 and the public composition API landed as ADR 0071. Still unsatisfied because no external application has been built and audited against it, and because agnara-http is not on an index, so an application cannot install it normally (see reference-apps-exist).
